651	    // MARK: - Kind → sections
652	
653	    /// The active sub-tab's sections, in the handoff's order. A section that
654	    /// does not apply is absent rather than disabled — the pane is rebuilt
655	    /// when the selection's kinds or the tab change, so there is nothing
656	    /// stale to grey out.
657	    ///
658	    /// Picture exists only for a selection with PIXELS: every control in it
659	    /// writes a `set_video` patch, and `InspectorBinding` addresses those to
660	    /// the clips that draw.
661	    override func makeSections() -> [InspectorSection] {
662	        let hasPixels = !binding.videoClips.isEmpty
663	        var sections: [InspectorSection] = []
664	        switch activeSubTab {
665	        case .text:
666	            sections = [
667	                textPane.contentSection(), textPane.fontSection(), textPane.styleSection(),
668	                textPane.outlineSection(), textPane.backdropSection(), textPane.boxSection(),
669	                textPane.animationSection(), textPane.presetSection(),
670	            ]
671	        case .shape:
672	            sections = [
673	                shapePane.shapeSection(), shapePane.strokeSection(), shapePane.fillSection(),
674	                // Immediately after Fill, because a gradient REPLACES a fill
675	                // when it is set and the two rows are read together.
676	                shapePane.gradientSection(), shapePane.arrowSection(),
677	            ]
678	        case .graphic:
679	            sections = [graphicPane.sourceSection()]
680	            if graphicPane.shared() != nil { sections.append(graphicPane.propertiesSection()) }
681	            sections.append(graphicPane.sizeSection())
682	            if binding.isSingle, let clip = binding.primary {
683	                sections.append(graphicPane.timelineSection(clip.id))
684	            }
685	        case .picture:
686	            sections = [videoPane.transformSection()]
687	            // Behind Subject right after Transform (road map creator-jobs CO5, CO-55).
688	            if videoPane.allBehindable { sections.append(videoPane.behindSubjectSection()) }
689	            // Layout after Behind Subject, before Crop (road map creator-jobs CO7, CO-71).
690	            if videoPane.allLayoutable { sections.append(videoPane.layoutSection(layoutState)) }
691	            if videoPane.allHideable { sections.append(videoPane.hideSilentSection()) }  // CO-94
692	            // `allSourcePixels` asks about the SOURCE KIND, so it says yes to
693	            // an audio-only file's clip too; the tab itself is what keeps a
694	            // crop off a clip that draws nothing.
695	            if videoPane.allSourcePixels {
696	                sections += [
697	                    videoPane.cropSection(), videoPane.cornerSection(), videoPane.chromaSection(),
698	                ]
699	                // Background right after Chroma Key (road map creator-jobs CO3, CO-30 (a)).
700	                if videoPane.allCutoutable { sections.append(videoPane.cutoutSection(cutoutMemo)) }
701	            }
702	            // Cursor after Background, before Shadow (road map creator-jobs CU3b, CU-38 (b)).
703	            if videoPane.allCursored { sections.append(videoPane.cursorSection()) }
704	            // Shadow is shared by all three drawing kinds, so it is here once.
705	            sections += [
706	                inspectorShadowSection(binding), videoPane.filtersSection(),
707	                videoPane.reflectionSection(), videoPane.spotlightSection(),
708	                videoPane.obscureSection(),
709	            ]
710	        case .color:
711	            // Light, then the Color section Picture used to hold (GR-2), then
712	            // Wheels (GR-11), Curves (GR-12), then Look (GR-7); Adjustment's
713	            // Strength first and the Qualifier second when every clip is an
714	            // adjustment clip (GR-6, GR-13).
715	            sections = [
716	                videoPane.lightSection(), videoPane.colorSection(), videoPane.wheelsSection(),
717	                videoPane.curvesSection(curveState),
718	            ]
719	            if videoPane.allAdjustment { sections.insert(videoPane.adjustmentSection(), at: 0) }
720	            if videoPane.allAdjustment { sections.insert(videoPane.qualifierSection(), at: 1) }
721	            sections.append(videoPane.lookSection(lookGallery))
722	        case .sound:
723	            sections = [
724	                audioPane.volumeSection(), audioPane.fadeSection(), audioPane.duckSection(),
725	                // The chain's head, in signal order (spec §11 AU-54, AU-38).
726	                audioPane.isolationSection(), audioPane.voiceSection(),
727	                audioPane.channelsSection(),
728	                audioPane.eqSection(), audioPane.humSection(),
729	                audioPane.noiseSection(), audioPane.gateSection(), audioPane.levellerSection(),
730	                audioPane.deEsserSection(),
731	                audioPane.compressorSection(), audioPane.mixSection(),
732	                // Last in the clip's chain, so last here (spec §11 AU-26).
733	                audioPane.limiterSection(),
734	            ]
735	        case .clip:
736	            if binding.isSingle, let clip = binding.primary {
737	                sections.append(timingSection(clip.id))
738	            } else if videoPane.allMedia {
739	                // The half of Timing a MULTI-clip selection can still answer
740	                // for: Reverse is a per-clip op that fans out happily, where
741	                // In, Out and Duration genuinely need one clip.
742	                sections.append(reverseTimingSection())
743	            }
744	            if videoPane.allMedia {
745	                sections.append(videoPane.speedSection())
746	            }
747	            if binding.isSingle, let clip = binding.primary,
748	               videoPane.overlap(before: clip) != nil {
749	                sections.append(videoPane.transitionSection(clip.id))
750	            }
751	            if hasPixels {
752	                sections.append(videoPane.motionSection())
753	            }
754	        }
755	        // A tab that would open as a column of shut headers opens its first
756	        // section with no stored preference instead. `expandByDefault` defers
757	        // to a section the user has closed themselves, so this is a default
758	        // and not an override — and it is offered to each section in TURN
759	        // because an id can be shared (`video.speed`, `clip.timing`), and a
760	        // group closed once elsewhere would otherwise leave the tab shut.
761	        if !sections.contains(where: { $0.isExpanded }) {
762	            for section in sections {
763	                if section.expandByDefault() { break }
764	            }
765	        }
766	        reveal.apply(sections, action: binding.selectedAction?.id, subTab: activeSubTab.rawValue)
767	        return sections
768	    }
769	}

5	/// One disclosure group: a header with the title, a right-aligned summary of
6	/// what the group currently says, an optional reset-to-default button, and the
7	/// rows. Collapsed state is per section id in `UserDefaults`, so a pane
8	/// rebuilt after every edit does not keep re-opening a group the user closed.
9	///
10	/// **The stored value records COLLAPSED, not expanded** — a section nobody has
11	/// touched has no stored value at all, which is what lets `defaultExpanded`
12	/// mean anything. Flipping that spelling would invert every saved panel.
13	final class InspectorSection: NSView {
14	    /// `UserDefaults` key prefix; the suffix is the section's stable id.
15	    static let collapsedKeyPrefix = "FrameJobInspectorSection."
16	
17	    let id: String
18	    let title: String
19	    let header = InspectorSectionHeader()
20	    private let content = NSStackView()
21	    private(set) var isExpanded = true
22	    private let summary: (() -> String?)?
23	    /// An explicit "differs from its default" (spec §11 CI-9), for a section
24	    /// whose rows do not read the props or whose Reset writes fewer keys
25	    /// than its rows read; nil folds the rows' own defaults.
26	    private let differs: (() -> Bool)?
27	    /// The rows' marks, folded (road map 9 §5) at the end of `init` and on
28	    /// every `refresh()`.
29	    private(set) var marks = SectionMarks.empty
30	    /// "Actions don't animate this" — shown while every row that writes is ⊘.
31	    private var inertNote: InspectorNoteLabel?
32	    /// The header's click, after the preference is stored — and nothing else:
33	    /// `reveal()` and `expandByDefault()` never call it (`KeyedReveal`).
34	    var didToggle: ((InspectorSection) -> Void)?
35	
36	    /// `summary` is a closure rather than a string because it is re-read on
37	    /// every `refresh()`: a collapsed section still has to tell the truth
38	    /// about the value under it. `defaultExpanded` is the state before the
39	    /// user has ever touched THIS section — the design opens Transform and
40	    /// the primary section of a text or shape selection, and closes the rest.
41	    init(
42	        id: String, title: String, summary: (() -> String?)? = nil,
43	        note: (() -> String?)? = nil, reset: (() -> Void)? = nil,
44	        differs: (() -> Bool)? = nil, defaultExpanded: Bool = true, rows: [NSView]
45	    ) {
46	        self.id = id
47	        self.title = title
48	        self.summary = summary
49	        self.differs = differs
50	        super.init(frame: .zero)
51	        let key = Self.collapsedKeyPrefix + id
52	        if let collapsed = UserDefaults.standard.object(forKey: key) as? Bool {
53	            isExpanded = !collapsed
54	        } else {
55	            isExpanded = defaultExpanded
56	        }
57	
58	        content.orientation = .vertical
59	        content.alignment = .leading
60	        content.spacing = InspectorMetrics.rowSpacing
61	        content.edgeInsets = NSEdgeInsets(
62	            top: 2, left: InspectorMetrics.inset, bottom: 8, right: InspectorMetrics.inset)
63	        let inert = InspectorNoteLabel { [weak self] in
64	            self?.marks.allNotAnimatable == true
65	                ? "Actions don't animate this. Edits here change the clip." : nil
66	        }
67	        inert.textColor = DS.textFaint
68	        inertNote = inert
69	        addRow(inert)
70	        if let note = note {
71	            addRow(InspectorNoteLabel(note: note))
72	        }
73	        for row in rows { addRow(row) }
74	
75	        header.configure(title: title, reset: reset, clear: { [weak self] in self?.clear() })
76	        header.onToggle = { [weak self] in self?.toggle() }
77	
78	        let stack = NSStackView(views: [header, content])
79	        stack.orientation = .vertical
80	        stack.alignment = .leading
81	        stack.spacing = 0
82	        stack.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
83	        addSubview(stack)
84	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
85	            stack.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor),
86	            stack.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor),
87	            stack.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: leadingAnchor),
88	            stack.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailingAnchor),
89	            header.widthAnchor.constraint(equalTo: stack.widthAnchor),
90	            content.widthAnchor.constraint(equalTo: stack.widthAnchor),
91	        ])
92	        content.isHidden = !isExpanded
93	        header.isExpanded = isExpanded
94	        for gutter in Self.gutters(in: content) { gutter.refresh() }
95	        foldMarks()
96	    }
97	
98	    @available(*, unavailable)
99	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
100	        fatalError("InspectorSection does not support NSCoder")
101	    }
102	
103	    private func addRow(_ row: NSView) {
104	        content.addArrangedSubview(row)
105	        row.widthAnchor.constraint(
106	            equalTo: content.widthAnchor, constant: -2 * InspectorMetrics.inset).isActive = true
107	    }
108	
109	    private func toggle() {
110	        isExpanded.toggle()
111	        // The redesign's one animation (spec §11 CI-15): through `DS.animate`,
112	        // which runs it unanimated under Reduce Motion. The state is set at once.
113	        DS.animate(DS.stateDuration) {
114	            content.isHidden = !isExpanded
115	            superview?.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
116	        }
117	        header.isExpanded = isExpanded
118	        UserDefaults.standard.set(!isExpanded, forKey: Self.collapsedKeyPrefix + id)
119	        didToggle?(self)
120	    }
121	
122	    /// Opens the section and writes NO preference — the selected action's
123	    /// auto-open (spec §11 CI-8), which must leave the person's own layout
124	    /// standing for when the action is left.
125	    func reveal() {
126	        isExpanded = true
127	        content.isHidden = false
128	        header.isExpanded = true
129	    }
130	
131	    /// Opens the section as a DEFAULT, for a pane that decided after building
132	    /// it that this is the group to open (`ClipPane`'s "the first section is
133	    /// open when there is no Transform"). `defaultExpanded` cannot say it: the
134	    /// pane only knows which section is first once it has them all.
135	    ///
136	    /// **It defers to the user and writes nothing.** A section the user has
137	    /// ever toggled has a stored value, and re-opening a group somebody closed
138	    /// on every rebuild would be worse than the closed panel this fixes;
139	    /// storing the state here would then make that override permanent.
140	    /// Returns whether it opened the section, so a caller walking a list can
141	    /// stop at the first one that had no stored preference.
142	    @discardableResult
143	    func expandByDefault() -> Bool {
144	        guard UserDefaults.standard.object(forKey: Self.collapsedKeyPrefix + id) == nil,
145	              !isExpanded
146	        else { return false }
147	        isExpanded = true
148	        content.isHidden = false
149	        header.isExpanded = true
150	        return true
151	    }
152	
153	    func refresh() {
154	        refreshOptionControls(in: content)
155	        foldMarks()
156	    }
157	
158	    /// The header's Clear (spec §11 CI-9): every key the section's rows
159	    /// write that the selected action holds, out of its end patch in ONE
160	    /// `set_action_end`.
161	    func clear() {
162	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
163	        guard let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap({ $0.binding }).first else { return }
164	        let keys = gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }
165	        binding.apply("Clear", binding.clearOps(keys))
166	    }
167	
168	    /// The rows' gutters, in the order `refreshOptionControls(in:)` walks.
169	    private static func gutters(in view: NSView) -> [InspectorMarkGutter] {
170	        view.subviews.flatMap { subview -> [InspectorMarkGutter] in
171	            if let gutter = subview as? InspectorMarkGutter { return [gutter] }
172	            return gutters(in: subview)
173	        }
174	    }
175	
176	    /// `marks` from the gutters as they stand, then the two things drawn from
177	    /// it: the ⊘ note and the header. A section is EDITING the selected
178	    /// action when any of its rows animates; one that none does (Document,
179	    /// Shape, a ⊘-only section) keeps its Reset, since its edits go to the
180	    /// clip.
181	    private func foldMarks() {
182	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
183	        let writing = gutters.filter { !$0.writes.isEmpty }
184	        let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap { $0.binding }.first
185	        marks = SectionMarks(
186	            keyed: gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }.count,
187	            other: gutters.contains {
188	                if case .other = $0.mark { return true } else { return false }
189	            },
190	            allNotAnimatable: !writing.isEmpty
191	                && writing.allSatisfy { $0.mark == .notAnimatable },
192	            differs: differs?() ?? gutters.contains { $0.default?.differs() == true },
193	            editing: gutters.contains { $0.animates } ? binding?.selectedActionNumber : nil)
194	        inertNote?.refresh()
195	        header.refresh(summary: summary?(), marks: marks)
196	    }
197	}

199	/// The auto-open (spec §11 CI-8): the sections the selected action keys are
200	/// revealed on the sub-tab showing them, remembered for as long as that
201	/// action stays selected — so a rebuild under the same action re-reveals
202	/// them, a sub-tab first shown later adds its own, and a header click that
203	/// closes one drops it. One per `ClipPane`, applied at the end of every
204	/// `makeSections()`; it lives here because `ClipPane.swift` is at its cap.
205	final class KeyedReveal {
206	    private(set) var action: UInt32?
207	    private(set) var seen: Set<String> = []
208	    private(set) var ids: Set<String> = []
209	
210	    func apply(_ sections: [InspectorSection], action: UInt32?, subTab: String) {
211	        guard let action else {
212	            (self.action, seen, ids) = (nil, [], [])
213	            return
214	        }
215	        if action != self.action { (self.action, seen, ids) = (action, [], []) }
216	        if !seen.contains(subTab) {
217	            seen.insert(subTab)
218	            ids.formUnion(sections.filter { $0.marks.keyed > 0 }.map(\.id))
219	        }
220	        for section in sections {
221	            section.didToggle = { [weak self] in self?.ids.remove($0.id) }
222	            if ids.contains(section.id) { section.reveal() }
223	        }
224	    }
225	}

315	        let editing = marks.editing
316	        clearButton?.isHidden = editing == nil || marks.keyed == 0
317	        clearButton?.toolTip = editing.map { "Remove this section from action \($0)" }
318	        resetButton?.isHidden = editing != nil || !marks.differs

324	        if resetButton?.isHidden == false { return "Reset" }

329	    /// (`DS.textMuted`, spec §11 CI-9) when the section differs from its

348	    override func updateTrackingAreas() {

350	        // Owner-filtered: a tooltip is a tracking area too (app/CLAUDE.md).
351	        for area in trackingAreas where area.owner === self { removeTrackingArea(area) }
352	        addTrackingArea(

366	    /// The state at once, the band's alpha through `DS.animate` — set
367	    /// directly inside it, never through `animator()`, which animates even
368	    /// outside a group and so would ignore Reduce Motion.
369	    private func setHovered(_ hovered: Bool) {
370	        guard hovered != isHovered else { return }
371	        isHovered = hovered
372	        DS.animate(DS.hoverDuration) {
373	            hoverBand.alphaValue = hovered ? 1 : 0

377	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
378	        // **Pitfall:** `DS.hoverFill` is `quaternaryLabelColor`, which is
379	        // ALREADY about 10% ink — taking 0.35 of it left a 3.5% wash that is
380	        // invisible in the light appearance, so the header did not separate
381	        // from the rows under it. Drawn at its own alpha it is a quiet band
382	        // that reads in both appearances.
383	        DS.hoverFill.setFill()
384	        bounds.fill()
385	        DS.border.setFill()
386	        NSRect(x: 0, y: bounds.height - 1, width: bounds.width, height: 1).fill()
387	
388	        let glyph = isExpanded ? "chevron.down" : "chevron.right"
389	        let box = NSRect(x: InspectorMetrics.inset, y: bounds.midY - 5, width: 10, height: 10)
390	        if let icon = NSImage(systemSymbolName: glyph, accessibilityDescription: title)?
391	            .withSymbolConfiguration(NSImage.SymbolConfiguration(pointSize: 9, weight: .semibold))
392	        {
393	            let tinted = icon.tinted(with: DS.textMuted)
394	            let size = tinted.size
395	            tinted.draw(
396	                in: NSRect(
397	                    x: box.minX, y: box.midY - size.height / 2, width: size.width,
398	                    height: size.height))
399	        } else {
400	            let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
401	                .font: DS.sans(9), .foregroundColor: DS.textMuted,
402	            ]
403	            (isExpanded ? "▾" : "▸").draw(
404	                at: NSPoint(x: box.minX, y: box.minY), withAttributes: attributes)
405	        }
406	
407	        let label = Self.titleLabel(title)
408	        label.draw(at: NSPoint(x: box.maxX + 6, y: bounds.midY - label.size().height / 2))
409	        drawSummary(after: drawMarks(after: box.maxX + 6 + label.size().width))
410	    }

412	    /// `◆N` in the action ink, then ◇ and ⊘ faint, after the title; answers
413	    /// where they end.
414	    private func drawMarks(after titleEnd: CGFloat) -> CGFloat {
415	        var x = titleEnd
416	        var parts: [(String, NSFont, NSColor)] = []
417	        if marks.keyed > 0 {
418	            parts.append(("◆\(marks.keyed)", DS.mono(9, weight: .medium), DS.action))
419	        }
420	        if marks.other { parts.append(("◇", DS.mono(9), DS.textFaint)) }
421	        if marks.allNotAnimatable { parts.append(("⊘", DS.mono(9), DS.textFaint)) }
422	        for (text, font, ink) in parts {
423	            let mark = NSAttributedString(
424	                string: text, attributes: [.font: font, .foregroundColor: ink])
425	            let size = mark.size()
426	            mark.draw(at: NSPoint(x: x + 6, y: bounds.midY - size.height / 2))
427	            x += 6 + size.width
428	        }
429	        return x
430	    }
431	
432	    /// The title in the micro-label FACE — mono 10, uppercase, 0.09em tracking
433	    /// — but not in the micro-label's ink.
434	    ///
435	    /// **Pitfall:** `DS.microLabel` paints in `DS.textFaint`
436	    /// (`tertiaryLabelColor`), which over this header's fill is grey on grey;
437	    /// with the Clip tab now stacking up to twenty collapsed headers, that
438	    /// reads as a list of DISABLED rows rather than a list of groups. Built
439	    /// here rather than by changing `DS.microLabel`, whose other callers draw
440	    /// one quiet label over the chrome, where faint is right. The summary
441	    /// beside it stays `textFaint`: it is secondary to the title.
442	    private static func titleLabel(_ title: String) -> NSAttributedString {
443	        let size: CGFloat = 10
444	        return NSAttributedString(
445	            string: title.uppercased(),
446	            attributes: [
447	                .font: DS.mono(size), .kern: size * 0.09, .foregroundColor: DS.textMuted,
448	            ])
449	    }
450	
451	    /// The state summary, right-aligned in whatever room is left between the
452	    /// title and the visible button. Truncated rather than clipped: it is a
453	    /// sentence fragment, and half a word with no ellipsis reads as a bug.
454	    private func drawSummary(after titleEnd: CGFloat) {
455	        guard let text = lastSummary, !text.isEmpty else { return }
456	        // A button that Auto Layout has not placed yet has a zero frame, and
457	        // taking its minX would put the summary's right edge at −6 and skip it
458	        // below. `refresh(summary:marks:)` only redraws when the summary or
459	        // the marks change, so a summary skipped on the first pass would stay
460	        // missing until one moved — hence the unplaced button falls back to
461	        // the inset.
462	        let visible = [clearButton, resetButton].compactMap { $0 }.first { !$0.isHidden }
463	        let button = visible.map { $0.frame.width > 0 ? $0.frame.minX : nil } ?? nil
464	        let right = (button ?? bounds.width - InspectorMetrics.inset) - 6
465	        let left = titleEnd + 8
466	        guard right - left > 14 else { return }
467	        let paragraph = NSMutableParagraphStyle()
468	        paragraph.alignment = .right
469	        paragraph.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
470	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
471	            .font: DS.mono(10), .foregroundColor: summaryInk,
472	            .paragraphStyle: paragraph,
473	        ]
474	        let height = text.size(withAttributes: attributes).height
475	        text.draw(
476	            in: NSRect(x: left, y: bounds.midY - height / 2, width: right - left, height: height),
477	            withAttributes: attributes)
478	    }
479	}

511	/// The five tabs, in strip order: the three of the chrome cleanup — the
512	/// selected CLIP, the project's media, the document itself — the Transcript
513	/// (spec §11 TX-20) and the Assistant (AI-4). The raw value is the strip
514	/// index, so the order is API: the Transcript's arrival moved the Assistant
515	/// from 3 to 4, and every reader goes through `.assistant` or `allCases`.
516	///
517	/// It was six — Video, Audio, Text, Shape, Media, Document — and four of those
518	/// were the same thing viewed four ways: the selected clip. Collapsing them
519	/// took the whole tab-visibility policy with it (a disabled tab, a preferred
520	/// tab, a pin to defeat the preference), because a Clip tab that lists the
521	/// sections the SELECTION actually has is always the right tab for a clip.
522	/// `ClipPane.makeSections()` is where that decision moved to.
523	///
524	/// The four kind tests below — three of them outlived the tabs they were
525	/// written for — are now what decides which sections the Clip tab shows.
526	enum InspectorTab: Int, CaseIterable {
527	    case clip, media, document, transcript, assistant
528	
529	    var title: String {
530	        switch self {
531	        case .clip: return "Clip"
532	        case .media: return "Media"
533	        case .document: return "Document"
534	        case .transcript: return "Transcript"
535	        case .assistant: return "Assistant"
536	        }
537	    }
538	
539	    /// Whether the clip puts pixels on the canvas — and the test that keeps
540	    /// an audio-only clip out of the video sections.
541	    static func hasPixels(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
542	        switch clip.source {
543	        case .text, .shape, .graphic, .nest, .adjustment:
544	            return true
545	        case .media, .still, .image:
546	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
547	            return media.hasVideo || media.kind == .image
548	        }
549	    }
550	
551	    /// Whether the clip carries live audio: its media has a track AND this
552	    /// half of the clip is enabled (Detach Audio flips that, §6).
553	    ///
554	    /// A nest clip has no media of its own, so the media test cannot answer
555	    /// for it — and "no" would be the wrong answer, because a nest clip's own
556	    /// volume, mute and fades MULTIPLY every voice inside it
557	    /// (`core/src/audio.rs`: turning a nest down turns everything in it
558	    /// down). What it is asked instead is whether it has audio properties at
559	    /// all, which is the core's own answer to the same question: `nest` gives
560	    /// the clip an `AudioProps` exactly when something inside it can make a
561	    /// sound (`edit_nest.rs`) and `set_audio` errors with "clip N has no
562	    /// audio properties" when it did not. Walking the contents here would be
563	    /// a second copy of that rule, free to drift from the one the writes go
564	    /// through.
565	    static func hasAudio(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
566	        guard clip.enabled.audio else { return false }
567	        if case .nest = clip.source { return clip.audio != nil }
568	        guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
569	        return media.hasAudio
570	    }
571	
572	    /// Whether the clip's rectangle comes from a decoded source — the clips
573	    /// that get Crop, Colour and Corner Radius. Text and shape clips get
574	    /// Transform, Opacity and Shadow only (§4.3).
575	    static func hasSourcePixels(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
576	        switch clip.source {
577	        case .media, .still, .image: return true
578	        case .text, .shape, .graphic, .nest, .adjustment: return false
579	        }
580	    }
581	
582	    /// Whether the clip is an adjustment clip (spec §11 GR-6): it draws
583	    /// nothing of its own and grades what is behind it, so it gets Color and
584	    /// Clip and never Picture.
585	    static func isAdjustment(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Bool {
586	        if case .adjustment = clip.source { return true }
587	        return false
588	    }
589	}

592	/// The row marks of the Clip inspector (road map 9 §5, spec §11 CI-7): what
593	/// the SELECTED action does to one row, in a 14 pt gutter before its label.
594	///
595	/// A row's mark is derived from two lists of `"group.key"` paths: the keys
596	/// its control WRITES — taken from the row's own `ops(read())` at build time,
597	/// so a write that lands on the action's end patch and one that lands on the
598	/// base props name the same key — and the keys it only FOLLOWS (Gain follows
599	/// Volume). Both empty is `.none`, action or no action: a row that says
600	/// nothing about what it writes (a readout, a Document-tab row) is never
601	/// marked ⊘ by omission.
602	enum RowMark: Equatable {
603	    /// Nothing to say — the gutter stays blank.
604	    case none
605	    /// ◆ — the row writes a key the selected action's end patch holds.
606	    case keyed
607	    /// ◆ and "at end" — the same, for a discrete control, which switches at
608	    /// the action's end rather than ramping.
609	    case keyedAtEnd
610	    /// ◇ — ANOTHER action keys it; the number is that action's time-order
611	    /// number (`ActionBands.ordered`).
612	    case other(Int)
613	    /// ○ — the row follows a keyed value without writing it.
614	    case follows
615	    /// ⊘ — the row writes the clip whatever is selected (CI-3, motion, a
616	    /// list's length): the selected action cannot animate it.
617	    case notAnimatable
618	}
619	
620	/// A section's marks, folded from its gutters: how many KEYS its rows write
621	/// that the selected action holds (CI-6's count, so a section's `◆N` agrees
622	/// with its sub-tab's), whether any row is ◇, whether every row that writes
623	/// is ⊘, whether the section differs from its default (spec §11 CI-9), and
624	/// the number of the action it is EDITING — the selected one, when any of
625	/// its rows animates — which is what turns its Reset slot into Clear.
626	struct SectionMarks: Equatable {
627	    var keyed: Int
628	    var other: Bool
629	    var allNotAnimatable: Bool
630	    var differs = false
631	    var editing: Int? = nil
632	
633	    static let empty = SectionMarks(keyed: 0, other: false, allNotAnimatable: false)
634	}
635	
636	/// A row's default (spec §11 CI-9): the undo name its reset runs under,
637	/// whether the row differs from its default now, and the ops that put the
638	/// default back — on the base props, or on the selected action's end.
639	struct InspectorRowDefault {
640	    let name: String
641	    let differs: () -> Bool
642	    let ops: () -> [ReelOp]
643	
644	    /// The default a typed row derives from its own `read` and `ops`: the
645	    /// value `read` answers in `.defaults`, written through `ops`.
646	    static func derived<T: Equatable>(
647	        _ binding: InspectorBinding, name: String, read: @escaping () -> T,
648	        ops: @escaping (T) -> [ReelOp]
649	    ) -> InspectorRowDefault {
650	        InspectorRowDefault(
651	            name: name,
652	            differs: { [weak binding] in
653	                guard let binding else { return false }
654	                return read() != binding.at(.defaults, read)
655	            },
656	            ops: { [weak binding] in
657	                guard let binding else { return [] }
658	                return ops(binding.at(.defaults, read))
659	            })
660	    }
661	}

663	/// The 14 pt column in front of every `inspectorRow`, blank at `.none`. It is
664	/// the row's FIRST subview, so `refreshOptionControls(in:)` refreshes it
665	/// before the row's controls — which is what lets its `refresh()` set the
666	/// label's ink and the controls' keyed border with nothing after it undoing
667	/// them (`OptionFieldControl.refresh()` never touches its layer).
668	///
669	/// Hovered while keyed (spec §11 CI-9) its ◆ draws as a × and a click on it
670	/// removes the row's keys from the selected action. The row sets `hovered`
671	/// (`InspectorRowView`), because the pointer is over the row, not the gutter.
672	final class InspectorMarkGutter: NSView, OptionControl {
673	    let writes: [String]
674	    let follows: [String]
675	    private(set) var mark: RowMark = .none
676	    private(set) weak var binding: InspectorBinding?
677	    let animates: Bool
678	    let `default`: InspectorRowDefault?
679	    private let discrete: Bool
680	    private weak var label: InspectorRowLabel?
681	    private let controls: [NSView]
682	
683	    /// ◆ or ◆ "at end".
684	    var isKeyed: Bool { mark == .keyed || mark == .keyedAtEnd }
685	    var hovered = false {
686	        didSet {
687	            guard hovered != oldValue else { return }
688	            needsDisplay = true
689	            updateToolTip()
690	        }
691	    }
692	    /// The × — hover alone is not enough, the row must be keyed.
693	    var showsRemove: Bool { hovered && isKeyed }
694	
695	    init(
696	        binding: InspectorBinding?, writes: [ReelOp], follows: [ReelOp],
697	        label: InspectorRowLabel?, controls: [NSView], discrete: Bool,
698	        default: InspectorRowDefault?
699	    ) {
700	        self.writes = InspectorBinding.paths(of: writes)
701	        self.follows = InspectorBinding.paths(of: follows)
702	        self.binding = binding
703	        self.animates = InspectorBinding.animates(writes)
704	        self.default = `default`
705	        self.discrete = discrete
706	        self.label = label
707	        self.controls = controls
708	        super.init(frame: .zero)
709	        translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
710	        widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorMetrics.markGutter).isActive = true
711	        refresh()
712	    }
713	
714	    @available(*, unavailable)
715	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
716	        fatalError("InspectorMarkGutter does not support NSCoder")
717	    }
718	
719	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
720	
721	    /// The keys this row writes that the selected action holds — what a
722	    /// section's `◆N` is the union of.
723	    func keyedWrites() -> Set<String> {
724	        guard let binding else { return [] }
725	        return binding.keyedPaths().intersection(writes)
726	    }
727	
728	    /// Takes the row's keys out of the selected action's end patch — the ×
729	    /// and the menu's "Remove from action N".
730	    func removeFromAction() {
731	        guard let binding else { return }
732	        binding.apply("Remove from Action", binding.clearOps(keyedWrites()))
733	    }
734	
735	    func refresh() {
736	        let next = binding?.mark(
737	            writes: writes, follows: follows, animates: animates, discrete: discrete) ?? .none
738	        if next != mark {
739	            mark = next
740	            needsDisplay = true
741	        }
742	        let ink = isKeyed ? DS.textStrong : mark == .notAnimatable ? DS.textFaint : DS.textMuted
743	        if let label, label.textColor != ink { label.textColor = ink }
744	        updateToolTip()
745	        paintBorders()
746	    }
747	
748	    private func updateToolTip() {
749	        if showsRemove, let number = binding?.selectedActionNumber {
750	            toolTip = "Remove from action \(number)"
751	        } else if case .other(let number) = mark {
752	            toolTip = "Changed by action \(number)"
753	        } else {
754	            toolTip = nil
755	        }
756	    }
757	
758	    /// The keyed rows' 1 pt action-ink border on their fields and popups.
759	    private func paintBorders() {
760	        let keyed = isKeyed
761	        for control in controls where control is OptionFieldControl
762	            || control is OptionPopupControl
763	        {
764	            if keyed { control.wantsLayer = true }
765	            guard let layer = control.layer else { continue }
766	            layer.borderWidth = keyed ? 1 : 0
767	            if keyed {
768	                effectiveAppearance.performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance {
769	                    layer.borderColor = DS.action.cgColor
770	                }
771	            }
772	        }
773	    }
774	
775	    /// A `CGColor` does not follow the appearance, so the border is resolved
776	    /// again when it changes.
777	    override func viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance() {
778	        super.viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance()
779	        paintBorders()
780	    }
781	
782	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
783	        guard showsRemove else {
784	            super.mouseDown(with: event)
785	            return
786	        }
787	        removeFromAction()
788	    }
789	
790	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
791	        let glyph: String
792	        let ink: NSColor
793	        switch mark {
794	        case .none: return
795	        case .keyed, .keyedAtEnd:
796	            (glyph, ink) = showsRemove ? ("×", DS.textMuted) : ("◆", DS.action)
797	        case .follows: (glyph, ink) = ("○", DS.action)
798	        case .other: (glyph, ink) = ("◇", DS.textFaint)
799	        case .notAnimatable: (glyph, ink) = ("⊘", DS.textFaint)
800	        }
801	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [.font: DS.mono(10), .foregroundColor: ink]
802	        let size = glyph.size(withAttributes: attributes)
803	        glyph.draw(
804	            at: NSPoint(x: (bounds.width - size.width) / 2, y: (bounds.height - size.height) / 2),
805	            withAttributes: attributes)
806	    }
807	}

890	extension InspectorBinding {
891	    /// The `"group.key"` paths a list of ops writes: `set_video`, `set_audio`
892	    /// and `set_text` by their patch's keys, `set_graphic` and an end's
893	    /// `graphic` by `graphicPaths`, `set_action_end` by each group of its
894	    /// patch, and `set_speed` by `speed`, the end's top-level rate key (spec
895	    /// §11 SR-21 (c)); every other op (a trim, a reverse) writes none.
896	    static func paths(of ops: [ReelOp]) -> [String] {
897	        let groups = ["set_video": "video", "set_audio": "audio", "set_text": "text"]
898	        var found = Set<String>()
899	        for op in ops {
900	            if op.name == "set_speed" {
901	                found.insert("speed")
902	                continue
903	            }
904	            guard let patch = op.args["patch"] as? [String: Any] else { continue }
905	            if let group = groups[op.name] {
906	                found.formUnion(patch.keys.map { group + "." + $0 })
907	            } else if op.name == "set_action_end" {
908	                found.formUnion(paths(inPatch: patch))
909	                found.formUnion(op.args["off"] as? [String] ?? [])  // keyed OFF (CI-14)
910	            } else if op.name == "set_graphic" { found.formUnion(graphicPaths(patch)) }
911	        }
912	        return found.sorted()
913	    }
914	
915	    /// An end patch's paths, spelled as `paths(of:)` spells them: a top-level
916	    /// key that is not a group — `speed` (spec §11 SR-21 (c)) — by its own
917	    /// name.
918	    private static func paths(inPatch patch: [String: Any]) -> [String] {
919	        patch.flatMap { group, value -> [String] in
920	            if group == "graphic" { return graphicPaths(value) }
921	            guard let fields = value as? [String: Any] else { return group == "speed" ? [group] : [] }
922	            return fields.keys.map { group + "." + $0 }
923	        }
924	    }
925	
926	    /// A `graphic` group's paths, `set_graphic`'s patch or an end's (spec §11
927	    /// G-34 (l)): `graphic.props.<key>` per prop, none for the core's
928	    /// `kinds`, and `graphic.<key>` for any other key — `set_graphic`'s
929	    /// `width`, `height` and `length`, which no end takes, so their rows are
930	    /// ⊘ while an action is selected.
931	    private static func graphicPaths(_ group: Any) -> [String] {
932	        guard let body = group as? [String: Any] else { return [] }
933	        var paths: [String] = []
934	        for (key, value) in body where key != "kinds" {
935	            if key == "props" {
936	                let props = (value as? [String: Any])?.keys.map { "graphic.props." + $0 }
937	                paths += props ?? []
938	            } else {
939	                paths.append("graphic." + key)
940	            }
941	        }
942	        return paths
943	    }
944	
945	    /// Whether any of the ops reaches an action's end patch.
946	    static func animates(_ ops: [ReelOp]) -> Bool {
947	        ops.contains { $0.name == "set_action_end" }
948	    }
949	
950	    /// The selected action's end patch, as paths.
951	    func keyedPaths() -> Set<String> {
952	        guard let action = selectedAction else { return [] }
953	        return Set(Self.paths(inPatch: action.end.dictionary))
954	    }
955	
956	    /// The time-order numbers of the single selected clip's OTHER actions
957	    /// whose end patch holds any of `paths`. One clip only: an action's
958	    /// number is its clip's, and two clips' numbers would say nothing.
959	    func otherActions(keying paths: [String]) -> [Int] {
960	        guard isSingle, let clip = primary, !paths.isEmpty else { return [] }
961	        let wanted = Set(paths)
962	        let selected = selectedAction?.id
963	        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).enumerated().compactMap { index, action in
964	            guard action.id != selected,
965	                  !wanted.isDisjoint(with: Self.paths(inPatch: action.end.dictionary))
966	            else { return nil }
967	            return index + 1
968	        }
969	    }
970	
971	    /// The selected action's time-order NUMBER on the single selected clip
972	    /// (`ActionBands.ordered`), nil with none selected.
973	    var selectedActionNumber: Int? {
974	        guard let id = selectedAction?.id, let clip = primary else { return nil }
975	        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).firstIndex { $0.id == id }.map { $0 + 1 }
976	    }
977	
978	    /// The id of the single selected clip's action numbered `number`.
979	    func actionID(number: Int) -> UInt32? {
980	        guard isSingle, let clip = primary else { return nil }
981	        let ordered = ActionBands.ordered(clip)
982	        return ordered.indices.contains(number - 1) ? ordered[number - 1].id : nil
983	    }
984	
985	    /// ONE `set_action_end` that nulls every `"group.key"` of `paths` in the
986	    /// selected action's end patch — a null REMOVES the key (spec §11 CI-9),
987	    /// so the value falls back to what was held. A one-part path (`speed`,
988	    /// spec §11 SR-21 (c)) is nulled at the patch's top. Nothing without a
989	    /// selected action on a single clip, or without a path.
990	    func clearOps(_ paths: Set<String>) -> [ReelOp] {
991	        guard let action = selectedAction, isSingle, let clip = primary, !paths.isEmpty
992	        else { return [] }
993	        var patch: [String: Any] = [:]
994	        for path in paths.sorted() {
995	            let parts = path.split(separator: ".", maxSplits: 1).map(String.init)
996	            if parts.count == 1 {
997	                patch[parts[0]] = NSNull()
998	                continue
999	            }
1000	            guard parts.count == 2 else { continue }
1001	            var group = patch[parts[0]] as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
1002	            if parts[0] == "graphic", parts[1].hasPrefix("props.") {
1003	                // An end's prop nests one level deeper (G-34 (a)).
1004	                var props = group["props"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
1005	                props[String(parts[1].dropFirst("props.".count))] = NSNull()
1006	                group["props"] = props
1007	            } else {
1008	                group[parts[1]] = NSNull()
1009	            }
1010	            patch[parts[0]] = group
1011	        }
1012	        guard !patch.isEmpty else { return [] }
1013	        return [.setActionEndRaw(clip: clip.id, action: action.id, patch: patch)]
1014	    }
1015	
1016	    /// Spec §11 CI-7's rule, in its order.
1017	    func mark(writes: [String], follows: [String], animates: Bool, discrete: Bool) -> RowMark {
1018	        if writes.isEmpty && follows.isEmpty { return .none }
1019	        if selectedAction != nil {
1020	            if !writes.isEmpty && !animates { return .notAnimatable }
1021	            let keyed = keyedPaths()
1022	            if !keyed.isDisjoint(with: writes) { return discrete ? .keyedAtEnd : .keyed }
1023	            if !keyed.isDisjoint(with: follows) { return .follows }
1024	        }
1025	        if let number = otherActions(keying: writes + follows).first { return .other(number) }
1026	        return .none
1027	    }
1028	
1029	    /// The value `read` answers at the PLAYHEAD, when the playhead is inside
1030	    /// the first selected clip; nil otherwise.
1031	    func nowValue(_ read: () -> Double) -> Double? {
1032	        guard let clip = primary, clip.start <= playhead, playhead < clip.end else { return nil }
1033	        return at(.playhead, read)
1034	    }
1035	
1036	    /// The value `read` answers at the selected action's START; nil with no
1037	    /// action selected.
1038	    func startValue(_ read: () -> Double) -> Double? {
1039	        guard selectedAction != nil else { return nil }
1040	        return at(.start, read)
1041	    }
1042	}

158	    /// The header's Clear (spec §11 CI-9): every key the section's rows
159	    /// write that the selected action holds, out of its end patch in ONE
160	    /// `set_action_end`.
161	    func clear() {
162	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
163	        guard let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap({ $0.binding }).first else { return }
164	        let keys = gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }
165	        binding.apply("Clear", binding.clearOps(keys))
166	    }

168	    /// The rows' gutters, in the order `refreshOptionControls(in:)` walks.
169	    private static func gutters(in view: NSView) -> [InspectorMarkGutter] {
170	        view.subviews.flatMap { subview -> [InspectorMarkGutter] in
171	            if let gutter = subview as? InspectorMarkGutter { return [gutter] }
172	            return gutters(in: subview)
173	        }
174	    }

176	    /// `marks` from the gutters as they stand, then the two things drawn from
177	    /// it: the ⊘ note and the header. A section is EDITING the selected
178	    /// action when any of its rows animates; one that none does (Document,
179	    /// Shape, a ⊘-only section) keeps its Reset, since its edits go to the
180	    /// clip.
181	    private func foldMarks() {
182	        let gutters = Self.gutters(in: content)
183	        let writing = gutters.filter { !$0.writes.isEmpty }
184	        let binding = gutters.lazy.compactMap { $0.binding }.first
185	        marks = SectionMarks(
186	            keyed: gutters.reduce(into: Set<String>()) { $0.formUnion($1.keyedWrites()) }.count,
187	            other: gutters.contains {
188	                if case .other = $0.mark { return true } else { return false }
189	            },
190	            allNotAnimatable: !writing.isEmpty
191	                && writing.allSatisfy { $0.mark == .notAnimatable },
192	            differs: differs?() ?? gutters.contains { $0.default?.differs() == true },
193	            editing: gutters.contains { $0.animates } ? binding?.selectedActionNumber : nil)
194	        inertNote?.refresh()
195	        header.refresh(summary: summary?(), marks: marks)
196	    }

200	/// revealed on the sub-tab showing them, remembered for as long as that
201	/// action stays selected — so a rebuild under the same action re-reveals
202	/// them, a sub-tab first shown later adds its own, and a header click that
203	/// closes one drops it. One per `ClipPane`, applied at the end of every
204	/// `makeSections()`; it lives here because `ClipPane.swift` is at its cap.
205	final class KeyedReveal {
206	    private(set) var action: UInt32?
207	    private(set) var seen: Set<String> = []
208	    private(set) var ids: Set<String> = []
209	
210	    func apply(_ sections: [InspectorSection], action: UInt32?, subTab: String) {
211	        guard let action else {
212	            (self.action, seen, ids) = (nil, [], [])
213	            return
214	        }
215	        if action != self.action { (self.action, seen, ids) = (action, [], []) }
216	        if !seen.contains(subTab) {
217	            seen.insert(subTab)
218	            ids.formUnion(sections.filter { $0.marks.keyed > 0 }.map(\.id))
219	        }
220	        for section in sections {
221	            section.didToggle = { [weak self] in self?.ids.remove($0.id) }
222	            if ids.contains(section.id) { section.reveal() }
223	        }
224	    }
225	}

511	/// The five tabs, in strip order: the three of the chrome cleanup — the
512	/// selected CLIP, the project's media, the document itself — the Transcript
513	/// (spec §11 TX-20) and the Assistant (AI-4). The raw value is the strip
514	/// index, so the order is API: the Transcript's arrival moved the Assistant
515	/// from 3 to 4, and every reader goes through `.assistant` or `allCases`.
516	///
517	/// It was six — Video, Audio, Text, Shape, Media, Document — and four of those
518	/// were the same thing viewed four ways: the selected clip. Collapsing them
519	/// took the whole tab-visibility policy with it (a disabled tab, a preferred
520	/// tab, a pin to defeat the preference), because a Clip tab that lists the
521	/// sections the SELECTION actually has is always the right tab for a clip.
522	/// `ClipPane.makeSections()` is where that decision moved to.
523	///
524	/// The four kind tests below — three of them outlived the tabs they were
525	/// written for — are now what decides which sections the Clip tab shows.
526	enum InspectorTab: Int, CaseIterable {
527	    case clip, media, document, transcript, assistant
528	
529	    var title: String {
530	        switch self {
531	        case .clip: return "Clip"
532	        case .media: return "Media"
533	        case .document: return "Document"
534	        case .transcript: return "Transcript"
535	        case .assistant: return "Assistant"
536	        }
537	    }
538	
539	    /// Whether the clip puts pixels on the canvas — and the test that keeps
540	    /// an audio-only clip out of the video sections.
541	    static func hasPixels(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
542	        switch clip.source {
543	        case .text, .shape, .graphic, .nest, .adjustment:
544	            return true
545	        case .media, .still, .image:
546	            guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
547	            return media.hasVideo || media.kind == .image
548	        }
549	    }
550	
551	    /// Whether the clip carries live audio: its media has a track AND this
552	    /// half of the clip is enabled (Detach Audio flips that, §6).
553	    ///
554	    /// A nest clip has no media of its own, so the media test cannot answer
555	    /// for it — and "no" would be the wrong answer, because a nest clip's own
556	    /// volume, mute and fades MULTIPLY every voice inside it
557	    /// (`core/src/audio.rs`: turning a nest down turns everything in it
558	    /// down). What it is asked instead is whether it has audio properties at
559	    /// all, which is the core's own answer to the same question: `nest` gives
560	    /// the clip an `AudioProps` exactly when something inside it can make a
561	    /// sound (`edit_nest.rs`) and `set_audio` errors with "clip N has no
562	    /// audio properties" when it did not. Walking the contents here would be
563	    /// a second copy of that rule, free to drift from the one the writes go
564	    /// through.
565	    static func hasAudio(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
566	        guard clip.enabled.audio else { return false }
567	        if case .nest = clip.source { return clip.audio != nil }
568	        guard let media = snapshot.media(for: clip) else { return false }
569	        return media.hasAudio
570	    }
571	
572	    /// Whether the clip's rectangle comes from a decoded source — the clips
573	    /// that get Crop, Colour and Corner Radius. Text and shape clips get
574	    /// Transform, Opacity and Shadow only (§4.3).
575	    static func hasSourcePixels(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
576	        switch clip.source {
577	        case .media, .still, .image: return true
578	        case .text, .shape, .graphic, .nest, .adjustment: return false
579	        }
580	    }
581	
582	    /// Whether the clip is an adjustment clip (spec §11 GR-6): it draws
583	    /// nothing of its own and grades what is behind it, so it gets Color and
584	    /// Clip and never Picture.
585	    static func isAdjustment(_ clip: ClipSnapshot) -> Bool {
586	        if case .adjustment = clip.source { return true }
587	        return false
588	    }
589	}

592	/// The row marks of the Clip inspector (road map 9 §5, spec §11 CI-7): what
593	/// the SELECTED action does to one row, in a 14 pt gutter before its label.
594	///
595	/// A row's mark is derived from two lists of `"group.key"` paths: the keys
596	/// its control WRITES — taken from the row's own `ops(read())` at build time,
597	/// so a write that lands on the action's end patch and one that lands on the
598	/// base props name the same key — and the keys it only FOLLOWS (Gain follows
599	/// Volume). Both empty is `.none`, action or no action: a row that says
600	/// nothing about what it writes (a readout, a Document-tab row) is never
601	/// marked ⊘ by omission.
602	enum RowMark: Equatable {
603	    /// Nothing to say — the gutter stays blank.
604	    case none
605	    /// ◆ — the row writes a key the selected action's end patch holds.

621	/// that the selected action holds (CI-6's count, so a section's `◆N` agrees
622	/// with its sub-tab's), whether any row is ◇, whether every row that writes
623	/// is ⊘, whether the section differs from its default (spec §11 CI-9), and
624	/// the number of the action it is EDITING — the selected one, when any of
625	/// its rows animates — which is what turns its Reset slot into Clear.

627	    var keyed: Int
628	    var other: Bool
629	    var allNotAnimatable: Bool
630	    var differs = false

636	/// A row's default (spec §11 CI-9): the undo name its reset runs under,
637	/// whether the row differs from its default now, and the ops that put the
638	/// default back — on the base props, or on the selected action's end.
639	struct InspectorRowDefault {
640	    let name: String
641	    let differs: () -> Bool
642	    let ops: () -> [ReelOp]
643	
644	    /// The default a typed row derives from its own `read` and `ops`: the
645	    /// value `read` answers in `.defaults`, written through `ops`.
646	    static func derived<T: Equatable>(
647	        _ binding: InspectorBinding, name: String, read: @escaping () -> T,
648	        ops: @escaping (T) -> [ReelOp]
649	    ) -> InspectorRowDefault {
650	        InspectorRowDefault(
651	            name: name,
652	            differs: { [weak binding] in
653	                guard let binding else { return false }
654	                return read() != binding.at(.defaults, read)
655	            },
656	            ops: { [weak binding] in
657	                guard let binding else { return [] }
658	                return ops(binding.at(.defaults, read))
659	            })

663	/// The 14 pt column in front of every `inspectorRow`, blank at `.none`. It is
664	/// the row's FIRST subview, so `refreshOptionControls(in:)` refreshes it
665	/// before the row's controls — which is what lets its `refresh()` set the
666	/// label's ink and the controls' keyed border with nothing after it undoing
667	/// them (`OptionFieldControl.refresh()` never touches its layer).
668	///
669	/// Hovered while keyed (spec §11 CI-9) its ◆ draws as a × and a click on it
670	/// removes the row's keys from the selected action. The row sets `hovered`
671	/// (`InspectorRowView`), because the pointer is over the row, not the gutter.
672	final class InspectorMarkGutter: NSView, OptionControl {
673	    let writes: [String]
674	    let follows: [String]
675	    private(set) var mark: RowMark = .none
676	    private(set) weak var binding: InspectorBinding?
677	    let animates: Bool
678	    let `default`: InspectorRowDefault?
679	    private let discrete: Bool
680	    private weak var label: InspectorRowLabel?
681	    private let controls: [NSView]

683	    /// ◆ or ◆ "at end".
684	    var isKeyed: Bool { mark == .keyed || mark == .keyedAtEnd }
685	    var hovered = false {
686	        didSet {
687	            guard hovered != oldValue else { return }
688	            needsDisplay = true
689	            updateToolTip()
690	        }
691	    }
692	    /// The × — hover alone is not enough, the row must be keyed.
693	    var showsRemove: Bool { hovered && isKeyed }

695	    init(
696	        binding: InspectorBinding?, writes: [ReelOp], follows: [ReelOp],
697	        label: InspectorRowLabel?, controls: [NSView], discrete: Bool,
698	        default: InspectorRowDefault?
699	    ) {
700	        self.writes = InspectorBinding.paths(of: writes)
701	        self.follows = InspectorBinding.paths(of: follows)
702	        self.binding = binding
703	        self.animates = InspectorBinding.animates(writes)
704	        self.default = `default`
705	        self.discrete = discrete
706	        self.label = label
707	        self.controls = controls
708	        super.init(frame: .zero)
709	        translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
710	        widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: InspectorMetrics.markGutter).isActive = true
711	        refresh()
712	    }
713	
714	    @available(*, unavailable)
715	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
716	        fatalError("InspectorMarkGutter does not support NSCoder")
717	    }
718	
719	    override var isFlipped: Bool { true }
720	
721	    /// The keys this row writes that the selected action holds — what a
722	    /// section's `◆N` is the union of.
723	    func keyedWrites() -> Set<String> {
724	        guard let binding else { return [] }
725	        return binding.keyedPaths().intersection(writes)
726	    }
727	
728	    /// Takes the row's keys out of the selected action's end patch — the ×
729	    /// and the menu's "Remove from action N".
730	    func removeFromAction() {
731	        guard let binding else { return }
732	        binding.apply("Remove from Action", binding.clearOps(keyedWrites()))
733	    }
734	
735	    func refresh() {
736	        let next = binding?.mark(
737	            writes: writes, follows: follows, animates: animates, discrete: discrete) ?? .none
738	        if next != mark {
739	            mark = next
740	            needsDisplay = true
741	        }
742	        let ink = isKeyed ? DS.textStrong : mark == .notAnimatable ? DS.textFaint : DS.textMuted
743	        if let label, label.textColor != ink { label.textColor = ink }
744	        updateToolTip()
745	        paintBorders()
746	    }
747	
748	    private func updateToolTip() {
749	        if showsRemove, let number = binding?.selectedActionNumber {
750	            toolTip = "Remove from action \(number)"
751	        } else if case .other(let number) = mark {
752	            toolTip = "Changed by action \(number)"
753	        } else {
754	            toolTip = nil
755	        }
756	    }
757	
758	    /// The keyed rows' 1 pt action-ink border on their fields and popups.
759	    private func paintBorders() {
760	        let keyed = isKeyed
761	        for control in controls where control is OptionFieldControl
762	            || control is OptionPopupControl
763	        {
764	            if keyed { control.wantsLayer = true }
765	            guard let layer = control.layer else { continue }
766	            layer.borderWidth = keyed ? 1 : 0
767	            if keyed {
768	                effectiveAppearance.performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance {
769	                    layer.borderColor = DS.action.cgColor
770	                }
771	            }
772	        }
773	    }
774	
775	    /// A `CGColor` does not follow the appearance, so the border is resolved
776	    /// again when it changes.
777	    override func viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance() {
778	        super.viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance()
779	        paintBorders()
780	    }
781	
782	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
783	        guard showsRemove else {
784	            super.mouseDown(with: event)
785	            return
786	        }
787	        removeFromAction()
788	    }
789	
790	    override func draw(_ dirtyRect: NSRect) {
791	        let glyph: String
792	        let ink: NSColor
793	        switch mark {
794	        case .none: return
795	        case .keyed, .keyedAtEnd:
796	            (glyph, ink) = showsRemove ? ("×", DS.textMuted) : ("◆", DS.action)
797	        case .follows: (glyph, ink) = ("○", DS.action)
798	        case .other: (glyph, ink) = ("◇", DS.textFaint)
799	        case .notAnimatable: (glyph, ink) = ("⊘", DS.textFaint)
800	        }
801	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [.font: DS.mono(10), .foregroundColor: ink]
802	        let size = glyph.size(withAttributes: attributes)
803	        glyph.draw(
804	            at: NSPoint(x: (bounds.width - size.width) / 2, y: (bounds.height - size.height) / 2),
805	            withAttributes: attributes)
806	    }
807	}

810	/// the coral "now …" of a field-only row. Hidden while `text` answers nil.
811	final class InspectorRowTag: NSTextField, OptionControl {
812	    private let text: () -> String?

815	        self.text = text

817	        isEditable = false
818	        isBordered = false
819	        isBezeled = false
820	        drawsBackground = false

830	    @available(*, unavailable)

832	        fatalError("InspectorRowTag does not support NSCoder")

838	        isHidden = next == nil

889	
890	extension InspectorBinding {
891	    /// The `"group.key"` paths a list of ops writes: `set_video`, `set_audio`
892	    /// and `set_text` by their patch's keys, `set_graphic` and an end's
893	    /// `graphic` by `graphicPaths`, `set_action_end` by each group of its
894	    /// patch, and `set_speed` by `speed`, the end's top-level rate key (spec
895	    /// §11 SR-21 (c)); every other op (a trim, a reverse) writes none.
896	    static func paths(of ops: [ReelOp]) -> [String] {
897	        let groups = ["set_video": "video", "set_audio": "audio", "set_text": "text"]
898	        var found = Set<String>()
899	        for op in ops {
900	            if op.name == "set_speed" {
901	                found.insert("speed")
902	                continue
903	            }
904	            guard let patch = op.args["patch"] as? [String: Any] else { continue }
905	            if let group = groups[op.name] {
906	                found.formUnion(patch.keys.map { group + "." + $0 })
907	            } else if op.name == "set_action_end" {
908	                found.formUnion(paths(inPatch: patch))
909	                found.formUnion(op.args["off"] as? [String] ?? [])  // keyed OFF (CI-14)
910	            } else if op.name == "set_graphic" { found.formUnion(graphicPaths(patch)) }
911	        }
912	        return found.sorted()
913	    }
914	
915	    /// An end patch's paths, spelled as `paths(of:)` spells them: a top-level
916	    /// key that is not a group — `speed` (spec §11 SR-21 (c)) — by its own
917	    /// name.
918	    private static func paths(inPatch patch: [String: Any]) -> [String] {
919	        patch.flatMap { group, value -> [String] in
920	            if group == "graphic" { return graphicPaths(value) }
921	            guard let fields = value as? [String: Any] else { return group == "speed" ? [group] : [] }
922	            return fields.keys.map { group + "." + $0 }
923	        }
924	    }
925	
926	    /// A `graphic` group's paths, `set_graphic`'s patch or an end's (spec §11
927	    /// G-34 (l)): `graphic.props.<key>` per prop, none for the core's
928	    /// `kinds`, and `graphic.<key>` for any other key — `set_graphic`'s
929	    /// `width`, `height` and `length`, which no end takes, so their rows are
930	    /// ⊘ while an action is selected.
931	    private static func graphicPaths(_ group: Any) -> [String] {
932	        guard let body = group as? [String: Any] else { return [] }
933	        var paths: [String] = []
934	        for (key, value) in body where key != "kinds" {
935	            if key == "props" {
936	                let props = (value as? [String: Any])?.keys.map { "graphic.props." + $0 }
937	                paths += props ?? []
938	            } else {
939	                paths.append("graphic." + key)
940	            }
941	        }
942	        return paths
943	    }
944	
945	    /// Whether any of the ops reaches an action's end patch.
946	    static func animates(_ ops: [ReelOp]) -> Bool {
947	        ops.contains { $0.name == "set_action_end" }
948	    }
949	
950	    /// The selected action's end patch, as paths.
951	    func keyedPaths() -> Set<String> {
952	        guard let action = selectedAction else { return [] }
953	        return Set(Self.paths(inPatch: action.end.dictionary))
954	    }
955	
956	    /// The time-order numbers of the single selected clip's OTHER actions
957	    /// whose end patch holds any of `paths`. One clip only: an action's
958	    /// number is its clip's, and two clips' numbers would say nothing.
959	    func otherActions(keying paths: [String]) -> [Int] {
960	        guard isSingle, let clip = primary, !paths.isEmpty else { return [] }
961	        let wanted = Set(paths)
962	        let selected = selectedAction?.id
963	        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).enumerated().compactMap { index, action in
964	            guard action.id != selected,
965	                  !wanted.isDisjoint(with: Self.paths(inPatch: action.end.dictionary))
966	            else { return nil }
967	            return index + 1
968	        }
969	    }
970	
971	    /// The selected action's time-order NUMBER on the single selected clip
972	    /// (`ActionBands.ordered`), nil with none selected.
973	    var selectedActionNumber: Int? {
974	        guard let id = selectedAction?.id, let clip = primary else { return nil }
975	        return ActionBands.ordered(clip).firstIndex { $0.id == id }.map { $0 + 1 }
976	    }
977	
978	    /// The id of the single selected clip's action numbered `number`.
979	    func actionID(number: Int) -> UInt32? {
980	        guard isSingle, let clip = primary else { return nil }
981	        let ordered = ActionBands.ordered(clip)
982	        return ordered.indices.contains(number - 1) ? ordered[number - 1].id : nil
983	    }
984	
985	    /// ONE `set_action_end` that nulls every `"group.key"` of `paths` in the
986	    /// selected action's end patch — a null REMOVES the key (spec §11 CI-9),
987	    /// so the value falls back to what was held. A one-part path (`speed`,
988	    /// spec §11 SR-21 (c)) is nulled at the patch's top. Nothing without a
989	    /// selected action on a single clip, or without a path.
990	    func clearOps(_ paths: Set<String>) -> [ReelOp] {
991	        guard let action = selectedAction, isSingle, let clip = primary, !paths.isEmpty
992	        else { return [] }
993	        var patch: [String: Any] = [:]
994	        for path in paths.sorted() {
995	            let parts = path.split(separator: ".", maxSplits: 1).map(String.init)
996	            if parts.count == 1 {
997	                patch[parts[0]] = NSNull()
998	                continue
999	            }
1000	            guard parts.count == 2 else { continue }
1001	            var group = patch[parts[0]] as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
1002	            if parts[0] == "graphic", parts[1].hasPrefix("props.") {
1003	                // An end's prop nests one level deeper (G-34 (a)).
1004	                var props = group["props"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:]
1005	                props[String(parts[1].dropFirst("props.".count))] = NSNull()
1006	                group["props"] = props
1007	            } else {
1008	                group[parts[1]] = NSNull()
1009	            }
1010	            patch[parts[0]] = group
1011	        }
1012	        guard !patch.isEmpty else { return [] }
1013	        return [.setActionEndRaw(clip: clip.id, action: action.id, patch: patch)]
1014	    }
1015	
1016	    /// Spec §11 CI-7's rule, in its order.
1017	    func mark(writes: [String], follows: [String], animates: Bool, discrete: Bool) -> RowMark {
1018	        if writes.isEmpty && follows.isEmpty { return .none }
1019	        if selectedAction != nil {
1020	            if !writes.isEmpty && !animates { return .notAnimatable }
1021	            let keyed = keyedPaths()
1022	            if !keyed.isDisjoint(with: writes) { return discrete ? .keyedAtEnd : .keyed }
1023	            if !keyed.isDisjoint(with: follows) { return .follows }
1024	        }
1025	        if let number = otherActions(keying: writes + follows).first { return .other(number) }
1026	        return .none
1027	    }
1028	
1029	    /// The value `read` answers at the PLAYHEAD, when the playhead is inside
1030	    /// the first selected clip; nil otherwise.
1031	    func nowValue(_ read: () -> Double) -> Double? {
1032	        guard let clip = primary, clip.start <= playhead, playhead < clip.end else { return nil }
1033	        return at(.playhead, read)
1034	    }
1035	
1036	    /// The value `read` answers at the selected action's START; nil with no
1037	    /// action selected.
1038	    func startValue(_ read: () -> Double) -> Double? {
1039	        guard selectedAction != nil else { return nil }
1040	        return at(.start, read)
1041	    }
1042	}

//! (spec §7.2).
//!
//! Swift hands each ramp to `AVMutableAudioMixInputParameters` as a linear
//! volume ramp over a time range, so everything that decides how loud a
//! composition audio track is at an instant — the clip's `volume`, its
//! `fade_in`/`fade_out`, volume ACTIONS, ducking from other clips, and the
//! four ways audio can be silenced (a muted clip, a muted track, a track
//! silenced by a solo elsewhere in its container, a clip with
//! `enabled.audio` false) — has to be folded into one piecewise-linear
//! function of project time before it crosses the FFI. AVFoundation has no
//! notion of "these ramps multiply".
//!
//! The shape of the computation is **sample, then simplify**:

//! 1. Collect BREAKPOINTS — every tick where the envelope can change slope
//!    or jump: clip edges, fade edges, duck edges, and a 1/30 s grid across
//!    every action that touches the audio group (an eased action is a
//!    curve, and a curve only becomes ramps by sampling it).

//!    once from the left, which is what lets a genuine jump — a clip
//!    starting at full volume, a duck with a zero-length release — survive
//!    as two ramp endpoints instead of being smeared into a slope.

29	//! start order — gaps between clips are ramps at 0, so the mix never plays
30	//! a track's ambient level under a hole in the timeline.
31	//!
32	//! Nothing here edits, and nothing here touches a sample: this is a
33	//! description of a gain curve, computed from the model alone.
34	//!
35	//! ### The crossfade
36	//!
37	//! An overlap whose transition says `audio: true` (format version 7) fades
38	//! its two clips across each other at CONSTANT POWER — `cos(p·π/2)` out,
39	//! `sin(p·π/2)` in, over the eased progress `transition.rs` reports. It is
40	//! one more factor in the product, so mute, solo, ducking, volume and the
41	//! fades all keep their precedence and a pair where only one clip has audio
42	//! still fades that one.
43	//!
44	//! Every STAGE multiplies its own term, which is where the sound parts
45	//! company with the picture: a clip inside an overlap inside a nest that is
46	//! itself in a transition gets BOTH fades, where `recipe.rs` picks the
47	//! clip's own transition and stops. That is right for sound — both fades
48	//! are audible — and the difference is deliberate rather than an oversight
49	//! in one of the two.
50	//!
51	//! TWO terms of the envelope are not properties of the voice being measured
52	//! at all, and each has a module of its own. Ducking, which a clip somewhere
53	//! ELSE in the project imposes, is `audio_duck.rs`; the crossfade above,
54	//! which the NEIGHBOUR this clip overlaps imposes, is `audio_crossfade.rs`,
55	//! both the gain at a tick and the breakpoints the curve has to be sampled
56	//! at. This module reads each as one more factor in the product, as it reads
57	//! any other.
58	//!
59	//! ### Nested sound
60	//!
61	//! What plays is not always a clip of `Project::clips`: a clip inside a nest
62	//! gets its own segment on a composition track (`nest.rs`), and neither its
63	//! props nor its track can be found by id in the project. So the envelope is
64	//! computed from [`Voice`]s rather than from clips — a voice being one
65	//! audible span plus every clip whose gain shapes it, innermost first. A
66	//! nested voice carries its own clip AND each nest clip it is inside,
67	//! because a nest clip's volume, fades, mute and muted track apply to
68	//! everything within: the stages MULTIPLY. That is what turning a nest down
69	//! means, and it is why the old shape — a list of `&Clip` looked up in the
70	//! project — could only ever have given nested audio full gain.

74	//! A solo is a mute on everyone else: while any track in a container's
75	//! track set has `solo`, every track in that set without it is silent, and
76	//! mute wins, so a track that is both muted and soloed stays silent
77	//! (`silenced`). The container is the timeline for a timeline track and
78	//! the nest's own tracks for a track inside a nest, so a nest's solo is

81	//! its enclosing stage, by the same multiply. The rule is on the SET, not

156	/// its own limit.
157	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
158	pub(crate) enum Side {
159	    /// The value AT the breakpoint — the start of the ramp that follows.
160	    Right,
161	    /// The limit approaching the breakpoint — the end of the ramp before.
162	    Left,
163	}
164	
165	pub(crate) fn covers(start: Ticks, end: Ticks, t: Ticks, side: Side) -> bool {
166	    match side {
167	        Side::Right => start <= t && t < end,
168	        Side::Left => start < t && t <= end,
169	    }
170	}

218	/// while some other track in `set` — its container's tracks — is. Mute

229	    /// The voice one flattened clip sings: itself, then the nest clips it is
230	    /// inside, outward.
231	    ///
232	    /// `top` is the timeline's track set, `Project::tracks`, which the
233	    /// instance does not carry: each stage's track is judged for solo among
234	    /// the tracks of ITS container, and for a stage at depth `d` — `d` nest
235	    /// clips above it — that container is the timeline when `d` is 0, else
236	    /// the nest the `d`th enclosing clip shows (`inside` is outermost
237	    /// first, so that is `inside[d - 1].nest`).
238	    pub(crate) fn of(top: &[Track], instance: &Instance<'a>) -> Voice<'a> {
239	        let set_at = |depth: usize| -> &[Track] {
240	            depth
241	                .checked_sub(1)
242	                .and_then(|i| instance.inside.get(i))
243	                .map_or(top, |enclosing| enclosing.nest.tracks.as_slice())
244	        };
245	        // The nest a stage at depth `d` sits IN — the same `inside[d - 1]`
246	        // the track set comes from, which is why the two are read together.
247	        let container_at = |depth: usize| -> Option<&'a Nest> {
248	            depth
249	                .checked_sub(1)
250	                .and_then(|i| instance.inside.get(i))
251	                .map(|enclosing| enclosing.nest)
252	        };
253	        let mut stages = Vec::with_capacity(instance.inside.len().saturating_add(1));
254	        stages.push(Stage {
255	            clip: instance.clip,
256	            origin: instance.origin,
257	            track_muted: silenced(set_at(instance.inside.len()), instance.track),
258	            container: container_at(instance.inside.len()),
259	            track_gain: track_gain(instance.track),
260	            track_pan: instance.track.pan,
261	        });
262	        for (depth, enclosing) in instance.inside.iter().enumerate().rev() {
263	            stages.push(Stage {
264	                clip: enclosing.clip,
265	                origin: enclosing.origin,
266	                track_muted: silenced(set_at(depth), enclosing.track),
267	                container: container_at(depth),
268	                track_gain: track_gain(enclosing.track),
269	                track_pan: enclosing.track.pan,
270	            });
271	        }
272	        Voice {
273	            start: instance.start,
274	            end: instance.end,
275	            stages,
276	        }
277	    }

286	/// Merges ramps that continue one another as a single straight line.
287	///
288	/// Sampling an action produces a run of short ramps; where the underlying
289	/// curve is straight (a linear action, or any stretch with no action at
290	/// all) they all lie on one line and the run collapses to one entry. The
291	/// test extends the first ramp's line across the second's span and asks
292	/// whether it lands on the second's end value, which bounds the error in
293	/// GAIN units — the thing that matters — rather than in slope units.
294	pub(crate) fn coalesce(ramps: Vec<Ramp>) -> Vec<Ramp> {
295	    let mut out: Vec<Ramp> = Vec::with_capacity(ramps.len());
296	    for ramp in ramps {
297	        // A zero-length ramp carries no information and AVFoundation
298	        // rejects an empty time range.
299	        if ramp.duration <= 0 {
300	            continue;
301	        }
302	        if let Some(last) = out.last_mut() {
303	            if joins(last, &ramp) {
304	                last.duration = last.duration.saturating_add(ramp.duration);
305	                last.to = ramp.to;
306	                continue;
307	            }
308	        }
309	        out.push(ramp);
310	    }
311	    out
312	}
313	
314	fn joins(a: &Ramp, b: &Ramp) -> bool {
315	    if a.duration <= 0 || b.duration <= 0 {
316	        return false;
317	    }
318	    // A jump between the two is a real event (a clip edge, a hard mute).
319	    if (a.to - b.from).abs() > JOIN_EPS {
320	        return false;
321	    }
322	    let total = a.duration.saturating_add(b.duration);
323	    let predicted = a.from + (a.to - a.from) / a.duration as f64 * total as f64;
324	    predicted.is_finite() && (predicted - b.to).abs() <= JOIN_EPS
325	}
