327	impl Project {
328	    /// The volume envelope for ONE composition audio track: `voices` are its
329	    /// segments (spec §7.2's A/B assignment guarantees they do not overlap),
330	    /// and `duckers` is every ducking clip in the project — this track's own
331	    /// are dropped here rather than by the caller.
332	    ///
333	    /// The returned ramps are in start order and tile the track's whole
334	    /// extent — first voice start to last voice end — with no gaps, so Swift
335	    /// can walk them straight into `setVolumeRamp(fromStartVolume:…)`
336	    /// without inventing anything in between. An empty input is an empty
337	    /// envelope.
338	    ///
339	    /// Folded in, in this order: the clip's `volume`; its fades; its volume
340	    /// actions; the same three for every nest clip it is inside; then
341	    /// ducking from every OTHER clip in the project whose `audio.duck` is
342	    /// set, multiplied over the whole thing. A clip that is silenced —
343	    /// `enabled.audio` false, `audio.muted`, or a track that is muted or
344	    /// silenced by a solo in its container, at any level — contributes 0
345	    /// over its extent, and so does a gap.
346	    pub fn audio_ramps(&self, voices: &[Voice<'_>], duckers: &[Ducker]) -> Vec<Ramp> {
347	        let mut own: Vec<&Voice> = voices.iter().filter(|v| v.end > v.start).collect();
348	        own.sort_by_key(|v| (v.start, v.clip_id()));
349	        let (Some(extent_start), Some(extent_end)) = (
350	            own.iter().map(|v| v.start).min(),
351	            own.iter().map(|v| v.end).max(),
352	        ) else {
353	            return Vec::new();
354	        };
355	        if extent_end <= extent_start {
356	            return Vec::new();
357	        }
358	
359	        // A clip does not duck the track it plays on: ducking exists to
360	        // lower the OTHER material, and a segment ducking its own neighbours
361	        // on one composition track would be a feedback loop with no
362	        // user-visible cause.
363	        let others: Vec<&Ducker> = duckers
364	            .iter()
365	            .filter(|d| !own.iter().any(|v| v.clip_id() == d.clip))
366	            .collect();
367	        let breaks = self.breakpoints(&own, &others, extent_start, extent_end);
368	
369	        let mut ramps: Vec<Ramp> = Vec::with_capacity(breaks.len());
370	        for pair in breaks.windows(2) {
371	            let (Some(&a), Some(&b)) = (pair.first(), pair.get(1)) else {
372	                continue;
373	            };
374	            if b <= a {
375	                continue;
376	            }
377	            ramps.push(Ramp {
378	                start: a,
379	                duration: b.saturating_sub(a),
380	                from: self.gain_at(&own, &others, a, Side::Right),
381	                to: self.gain_at(&own, &others, b, Side::Left),
382	            });
383	        }
384	        coalesce(ramps)
385	    }
386	
387	    /// The ticks the envelope is sampled at: the ends of the extent, every
388	    /// voice edge, every fade edge of every stage, every duck edge, and a
389	    /// 1/30 s grid inside each action that touches the audio group. Sorted,
390	    /// deduplicated, and clipped to the extent, so the ramps built from
391	    /// consecutive entries tile it exactly.
392	    fn breakpoints(
393	        &self,
394	        voices: &[&Voice<'_>],
395	        duckers: &[&Ducker],
396	        extent_start: Ticks,
397	        extent_end: Ticks,
398	    ) -> Vec<Ticks> {
399	        let mut breaks: Vec<Ticks> = vec![extent_start, extent_end];
400	
401	        for voice in voices {
402	            // The voice's own edges, which for a nested clip are the nest
403	            // clip's edges as much as its own.
404	            breaks.push(voice.start);
405	            breaks.push(voice.end);
406	            for stage in &voice.stages {
407	                let clip = stage.clip;
408	                let end = stage.origin.saturating_add(clip.duration);
409	                breaks.push(stage.origin);
410	                breaks.push(end);
411	                // Fades come from the base props. If an action animates a
412	                // fade length the action's own samples below carry the
413	                // change; the fade edges are only a promise that the two
414	                // obvious corners are breakpoints.
415	                let props = clip.audio.unwrap_or_default();
416	                if props.fade_in > 0 {
417	                    let edge = stage.origin.saturating_add(props.fade_in);
418	                    breaks.push(edge);
419	                    // A shaped fade is a curve, sampled like an eased action
420	                    // (spec §11 AU-114); its shape read where the fade runs.
421	                    let shapes = [0, props.fade_in].map(|c| self.audio_props_at(clip, c));
422	                    if shapes.iter().any(|p| !p.fade_in_shape.is_linear()) {
423	                        breaks.extend(fade_breaks(stage.origin, edge));
424	                    }
425	                }
426	                if props.fade_out > 0 {
427	                    let edge = end.saturating_sub(props.fade_out);
428	                    breaks.push(edge);
429	                    let from = clip.duration.saturating_sub(props.fade_out);
430	                    let shapes = [from, clip.duration].map(|c| self.audio_props_at(clip, c));
431	                    if shapes.iter().any(|p| !p.fade_out_shape.is_linear()) {
432	                        breaks.extend(fade_breaks(edge, end));
433	                    }
434	                }
435	
436	                // The crossfade is a curve too, and an eased one is not even
437	                // a straight line, so an audio-true overlap gets its two
438	                // edges plus samples across it. The step is the ACTION
439	                // loop's own formula below, which is what keeps a
440	                // twenty-minute overlap to ~4096 points rather than 36,000.
441	                if let Some(overlap_breaks) = self.crossfade_breaks(stage) {
442	                    breaks.extend(overlap_breaks);
443	                }
444	
445	                for action in &clip.actions {
446	                    // Only the audio group can move the envelope: an action
447	                    // interpolates the whole state toward its patch, so a
448	                    // patch that never mentions `audio` leaves the gain
449	                    // exactly constant across its span and needs no samples.
450	                    if action.duration <= 0 || action.end.get("audio").is_none() {
451	                        continue;
452	                    }
453	                    let start = stage.origin.saturating_add(action.start);
454	                    let end = start.saturating_add(action.duration);
455	                    breaks.push(start);
456	                    breaks.push(end);
457	                    let step = ACTION_SAMPLE.max(action.duration / MAX_ACTION_SAMPLES + 1);
458	                    let mut t = start.saturating_add(step);
459	                    while t < end {
460	                        breaks.push(t);
461	                        t = t.saturating_add(step);
462	                    }
463	                }
464	            }
465	        }
466	
467	        for ducker in duckers {
468	            if let Some(spans) = &ducker.spans {
469	                breaks.extend(speech_breaks(ducker, spans));
470	                continue;
471	            }
472	            breaks.push(ducker.start);
473	            breaks.push(ducker.start.saturating_add(ducker.duck.attack.max(0)));
474	            breaks.push(ducker.end);
475	            breaks.push(ducker.end.saturating_add(ducker.duck.release.max(0)));
476	        }
477	
478	        breaks.retain(|t| *t >= extent_start && *t <= extent_end);
479	        breaks.sort_unstable();
480	        breaks.dedup();
481	        breaks
482	    }

484	    /// The whole track's gain at one instant: the covering segment's own
485	    /// gain (0 in a gap) times every ducker's multiplier.
486	    fn gain_at(&self, voices: &[&Voice<'_>], duckers: &[&Ducker], t: Ticks, side: Side) -> f64 {
487	        // Segments on one composition track never overlap, so the first
488	        // covering voice is the only one; `find` on the start-ordered list
489	        // keeps a hand-written overlap deterministic rather than summing
490	        // two clips into a gain nobody asked for.
491	        let mut gain = voices
492	            .iter()
493	            .find(|v| covers(v.start, v.end, t, side))
494	            .map(|v| self.voice_gain(v, t, side))
495	            .unwrap_or(0.0);
496	        for ducker in duckers {
497	            gain *= duck_gain(ducker, t, side);
498	        }
499	        gain
500	    }
501	
502	    /// One voice's gain: its clip's own, times that of every nest clip it is
503	    /// inside. Turning a nest down turns everything in it down, and muting
504	    /// one silences everything in it — which falls out of the product rather
505	    /// than needing a rule of its own.
506	    fn voice_gain(&self, voice: &Voice<'_>, t: Ticks, side: Side) -> f64 {
507	        let mut gain = 1.0;
508	        for stage in &voice.stages {
509	            if gain == 0.0 {
510	                break;
511	            }
512	            gain *= self.stage_gain(stage, t, side);
513	        }
514	        gain
515	    }
516	
517	    /// One clip's own gain at project time `t`: its evaluated volume shaped
518	    /// by its fades, times its track's volume (AU-103), or 0 if it is
519	    /// silenced.
520	    fn stage_gain(&self, stage: &Stage<'_>, t: Ticks, side: Side) -> f64 {
521	        let clip = stage.clip;
522	        if !clip.enabled.audio {
523	            return 0.0;
524	        }
525	        // A muted TRACK — or one a solo elsewhere has silenced — still gets
526	        // its segments in the composition: the plan does not change when
527	        // the user unmutes or un-solos (spec §7.2), so the silence has to
528	        // show up here, as a zero envelope.
529	        if stage.track_muted {
530	            return 0.0;
531	        }
532	
533	        let clip_t = t.saturating_sub(stage.origin);
534	        let props = self.audio_props_at(clip, clip_t);
535	        if props.muted {
536	            return 0.0;
537	        }
538	        // The NaN branch is unreachable defence: JSON carries no NaN, a
539	        // base volume out of range is refused by `check_audio`, and the
540	        // actions path has already run `clamp_audio`, which maps NaN to 1.
541	        // Its 0 is the gain of a silenced clip, a different question from
542	        // a prop's neutral.
543	        let mut gain = if props.volume.is_finite() {
544	            props.volume.clamp(0.0, MAX_GAIN)
545	        } else {
546	            0.0
547	        };
548	
549	        // Fades are ramps from 0 and to 0 at the clip's OWN edges, in clip
550	        // time, so they follow the clip when it moves and shrink with a
551	        // trim only when the user shortens them. A fade longer than the
552	        // clip, or a pair that overlaps, multiplies — the honest reading of
553	        // "both are in effect here" and a dip rather than a discontinuity.
554	        if props.fade_in > 0 && clip_t < props.fade_in {
555	            let u = (clip_t.max(0) as f64 / props.fade_in as f64).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
556	            gain *= props.fade_in_shape.gain(u);
557	        }
558	        let fade_out_start = clip.duration.saturating_sub(props.fade_out.max(0));
559	        if props.fade_out > 0 && clip_t > fade_out_start {
560	            let remaining = clip.duration.saturating_sub(clip_t).max(0) as f64;
561	            gain *= props
562	                .fade_out_shape
563	                .gain((remaining / props.fade_out as f64).clamp(0.0, 1.0));
564	        }
565	
566	        gain * stage.track_gain * self.crossfade_gain(stage, t, side)
567	    }
568	
569	    /// The clip's audio props at a clip time, through its actions.
570	    ///
571	    /// The fast path matters: [`Project::audio_ramps`] asks for this at
572	    /// every breakpoint, and a clip with no actions has the same props at
573	    /// all of them, so the serialize/deserialize round trip in
574	    /// `evaluate_clip` is skipped entirely for the common case.
575	    fn audio_props_at(&self, clip: &Clip, clip_t: Ticks) -> AudioProps {
576	        if clip.actions.is_empty() {
577	            return clip.audio.unwrap_or_default();
578	        }
579	        self.evaluate_clip(clip, clip_t).audio
580	    }
581	}
582	//! Fade and crossfade shapes (spec §11 AU-114, AU-115): the gain a
583	//! [`FadeShape`] gives at a progress, and the ticks a shaped fade has to be
584	//! sampled at for its curve to survive `audio.rs`'s coalescing.
585	//!
586	//! A shape is a curve over the fade's progress u in 0..1, read by
587	//! `audio.rs`'s fades (u is `t / fade_in` in, `remaining / fade_out` out) and
588	//! by `audio_crossfade.rs` over a transition's eased progress. `linear` is
589	//! `u` itself — the expression the fades always used, so a linear fade
590	//! plans exactly as before and needs no samples — and the other three are
591	//! not straight lines, so a fade in one of them is sampled on the action
592	//! grid, as an eased action is.
593	//!
594	//! It also holds [`Transition`]'s `Default`, because the one field that keeps
595	//! it from being derived is a shape: a transition's file default crossfades
596	//! (when `audio` is on) at R5-2's constant power, `plus_3db`, where a fade's
597	//! default is `linear`.
598	
599	use std::f64::consts::{FRAC_PI_2, PI};
600	
601	use crate::audio::{ACTION_SAMPLE, MAX_ACTION_SAMPLES};
602	use crate::model::{Curve, FadeShape, Transition, TransitionKind};
603	use crate::time::Ticks;
604	
605	impl FadeShape {
606	    /// The gain at progress `u`, clamped to 0..1: Linear `u`, S-curve
607	    /// `(1 − cos πu)/2`, +3 dB `sin(uπ/2)`, −3 dB `1 − cos(uπ/2)`. Each runs
608	    /// from exactly 0 to exactly 1 at the two ends, so a fade never leaves a
609	    /// residue of gain where it should be silent or full.
610	    pub(crate) fn gain(self, u: f64) -> f64 {
611	        match self {
612	            FadeShape::Linear => u,
613	            _ if u <= 0.0 => 0.0,
614	            _ if u >= 1.0 => 1.0,
615	            FadeShape::SCurve => (1.0 - (PI * u).cos()) / 2.0,
616	            FadeShape::Plus3Db => (u * FRAC_PI_2).sin(),
617	            FadeShape::Minus3Db => 1.0 - (u * FRAC_PI_2).cos(),
618	        }
619	    }
620	}
621	
622	/// The ticks a shaped fade over `[start, end]` (project time) is sampled at:
623	/// its two edges plus the action grid across it — `ACTION_SAMPLE`, widened
624	/// so one fade never contributes more than `MAX_ACTION_SAMPLES` points, the
625	/// step `audio.rs`'s action loop and `audio_crossfade.rs` both use.
626	pub(crate) fn fade_breaks(start: Ticks, end: Ticks) -> Vec<Ticks> {
627	    let mut out = vec![start, end];
628	    let span = end.saturating_sub(start);
629	    if span <= 0 {
630	        return out;
631	    }
632	    let step = ACTION_SAMPLE.max(span / MAX_ACTION_SAMPLES + 1);
633	    let mut t = start.saturating_add(step);
634	    while t < end {
635	        out.push(t);
636	        t = t.saturating_add(step);
637	    }
638	    out
639	}

654	//! A track's own terms on the sound that plays through it (format version 35,
655	//! spec §11 AU-102..AU-104): its fader as a gain and its pan as a list the
656	//! plan carries.
657	//!
658	//! **Volume** is an envelope term, read by `audio.rs` exactly where the
659	//! track's mute is: each [`crate::audio::Stage`] carries its track's gain,
660	//! decided in `Voice::of`'s walk because a nested clip's track is not in
661	//! `Project::tracks`, and `stage_gain` multiplies it after the mute. So a
662	//! nested clip is scaled by its own track and by every enclosing nest clip's
663	//! track, the stages multiplying as their volumes do.
664	//!
665	//! **Pan** cannot be a gain curve — it needs both channels — so it travels in
666	//! the plan as an audio segment's `track_pans`, and the app's tap applies the
667	//! product of their constant-power pairs as a balance, after the clip's own

769	/// Whether `action`'s end names any tap key in its `audio` object.
770	pub(crate) fn names_tap_key(action: &Action) -> bool {
771	    action
772	        .end
773	        .get("audio")
774	        .and_then(Value::as_object)
775	        .is_some_and(|audio| TAP_KEYS.iter().any(|key| audio.contains_key(*key)))

778	/// `audio` cut to [`TAP_KEYS`], in their order.
779	fn tap_keys(audio: &Value) -> Value {
780	    let mut out = Map::new();
781	    for key in TAP_KEYS {
782	        if let Some(value) = audio.get(key) {
783	            out.insert(key.to_string(), value.clone());
784	        }
785	    }
786	    Value::Object(out)
787	}

790	    /// The automation of the segment `voice` plays (AU-85): empty when its

792	    /// voice's two ends, each such action's two ends and, inside a
793	    /// non-linear one, the envelope's own 1/30 s grid (`audio.rs`'s
794	    /// `breakpoints`), clipped to the voice, sorted and deduplicated.
795	    pub(crate) fn automation(&self, voice: &Voice<'_>) -> Vec<AutomationPoint> {
796	        let Some(stage) = voice.stages.first() else {
797	            return Vec::new();
798	        };
799	        let clip = stage.clip;
800	        let actions: Vec<&Action> = clip
801	            .actions
802	            .iter()
803	            .filter(|a| a.duration > 0 && names_tap_key(a))
804	            .collect();
805	        if actions.is_empty() || voice.end <= voice.start {
806	            return Vec::new();
807	        }
808	        let mut ticks: Vec<Ticks> = vec![voice.start, voice.end];
809	        for action in actions {
810	            let start = stage.origin.saturating_add(action.start);
811	            let end = start.saturating_add(action.duration);
812	            ticks.push(start);
813	            ticks.push(end);
814	            if action.curve == Curve::Linear {
815	                continue;
816	            }
817	            let step = ACTION_SAMPLE.max(action.duration / MAX_ACTION_SAMPLES + 1);
818	            let mut t = start.saturating_add(step);
819	            while t < end {
820	                ticks.push(t);
821	                t = t.saturating_add(step);
822	            }
823	        }
824	        ticks.retain(|t| *t >= voice.start && *t <= voice.end);
825	        ticks.sort_unstable();
826	        ticks.dedup();
827	        ticks
828	            .into_iter()
829	            .map(|at| {
830	                let evaluated = self.evaluate_clip(clip, at.saturating_sub(stage.origin));
831	                AutomationPoint {
832	                    at,
833	                    audio: tap_keys(&audio_json(&evaluated.audio)),
834	                }
835	            })
836	            .collect()
837	    }

842	//!
843	//! `isolation` is written only when not 0 in the file (format 31), so
844	//! `to_json` leaves a clip with none without the key — and `lerp` walks only
845	//! its FROM side's keys, so an action toward 0.8 would hold 0 for its whole
846	//! span and jump at the end. [`audio_json`] writes it, as `color_json` writes
847	//! tone's neutral keys.
848	//!
849	//! The EQ's two slopes (12 or 24 dB/octave), the hum's mains (50 or 60 Hz)
850	//! and its harmonics are integers in the schema, so `lerp_number` would
851	//! round them through every value between — a 12 → 24 slope passing 18,
852	//! which no stage designs, and a 50 → 60 mains passing 55. They are choices,
853	//! not quantities: [`hold_audio_steps`] holds each at its start value until
854	//! the action's end, which is §5.4's rule for a switch.

857	//! gain curve, made ahead of time from the clip's loudness (AU-66): a
858	//! response between two curves has none, so it switches at the end too.

865	/// A clip's audio group as JSON with `isolation` present at 0 (AU-86).
866	pub(crate) fn audio_json(audio: &AudioProps) -> Value {
867	    let mut value = to_json(audio);
868	    if let Value::Object(fields) = &mut value {
869	        if !fields.contains_key("isolation") {
870	            fields.insert("isolation".to_string(), to_json(&audio.isolation));
871	        }
872	    }
873	    value
874	}

876	/// The audio numbers that switch at an action's end rather than glide
877	/// (AU-86), as JSON pointers into the evaluated state.
878	pub(crate) const HELD_AUDIO_NUMBERS: [&str; 5] = [
879	    "/audio/eq/high_pass/slope",
880	    "/audio/eq/low_pass/slope",
881	    "/audio/hum/frequency",
882	    "/audio/hum/harmonics",
883	    "/audio/leveller/response",
884	];

886	/// Puts each [`HELD_AUDIO_NUMBERS`] field of `lerped` back to its value in
887	/// `from`, the state the spanning action started from. Only where both have
888	/// it: a slot present on one side alone already holds or switches whole
889	/// through `lerp`'s mismatched-type rule.
890	pub(crate) fn hold_audio_steps(from: &Value, lerped: &mut Value) {
891	    for pointer in HELD_AUDIO_NUMBERS {
892	        let Some(start) = from.pointer(pointer) else {
893	            continue;
894	        };

896	            *slot = start.clone();
897	        }

canvas-and-layers.md:664:  the ramp already has there. A gradient can have up to **eight** stops.
audio.md:3:Frame Job mixes sound from every clip that has it: a camera clip, an audio-only file, a microphone recording or a nest. Each clip has its own level, fades, ducking, voice isolation, a voice effect, channel choice, EQ, hum removal, noise reduction, gate, leveller, de-esser, compressor, pan and mono fold, and a true-peak limiter, and each track can be muted or soloed and has its own volume, pan, compressor and limiter. Four commands do the measuring for you. Normalize sets a clip's level from its loudness (or its loudest moment), Enhance Voice sets a voice recording up for speech from its own measurements, Match Audio gives clips another clip's loudness and tone, and Synchronize Audio lines up a camera and a separate recorder by their sound. The preview and the export use the same mix, so what you hear while editing is what gets written, except that every export also holds its peaks under −1 dBTP with a master limiter the preview doesn't have, and a track's compressor and limiter are exact in an export but approximate in the preview (see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter)).
audio.md:92:- **⌥-click the line** to add a point there. A point is an action, not a keyframe: Frame Job adds an action that runs from the end of the previous action (or the clip's start) to where you clicked, ending at the level the line already has there, so the click on its own changes nothing you hear. Keep the mouse down and drag to move the new point's level. Inside an action that changes only the volume, the click splits that action in two at the point instead. Both halves keep its curve, so a linear action sounds the same until you drag, while an eased one is eased again on each side of the point. The click beeps, and adds nothing, inside an action that also changes something else or that runs past the clip's end (as one can after a trim), or within one frame of the start of the action it is in or of the previous action's end. Adding a point is one undo step, "Add Volume Point".
audio.md:111:- **It can go past 400 %.** A quiet recording, such as a desktop USB microphone's, is turned up as far as it needs, up to the 3200 % ceiling (about +30 dB). Only a clip whose peak is quieter than about −31 dBFS can't reach −1 dBFS. It is turned up to 3200 % and stops there.
audio.md:174:The shapes are always the clip's own setting, even with an action selected. It travels with the clip when you move it, and it stays at the edge when you trim. Where a fade in and a fade out overlap, or a fade is longer than the clip, the two multiply, which gives a dip in the middle rather than a jump.
audio.md:180:- The fade length snaps to whole frames and can't be longer than the clip.
audio.md:207:With **Clip Length**, ducking follows the clip's length on the timeline, not whether anyone is talking. The other audio stays lowered for the whole length of the ducking clip, through pauses, and comes back up only after the clip ends. You can therefore see exactly when ducking applies by looking at the timeline. If the attack is longer than the clip, the level never fully reaches Level, and the release starts from wherever it got to.
audio.md:243:*Agents:* `set_audio` with `isolation` from 0 to 1 (0 is off). The render's status isn't in `get_project`; an export waits for it.
audio.md:329:*Agents:* `set_audio` with `noise_reduction` from 0 to 1.
audio.md:419:Each clip's limiter holds that clip alone. Every export also runs a **master limiter** over the whole mix, the same kind of limiter at −1 dBTP (or the export's own ceiling), so two limited clips crossfading, a nest turned up or an action raising a clip's volume still can't take the file past it. The preview has no master limiter. See [Exporting](export.md#loudness).
audio.md:552:A track can have its own **compressor** and **limiter**, below Pan in the same panel (the fifth header switch, **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu, or **Track ▸ Mix…**). They act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter, whose ceiling is the highest true peak the track hands the mix.
audio.md:570:- **Exact in every export.** An export plays each track with a compressor or limiter through it on its own before the tracks are mixed, and a stem of that track includes them. The master limiter still runs over the mix afterwards.
audio.md:616:The figures are the mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness setting and its master limiter, and the column says so. While any track has a compressor or limiter, it says they are approximate (see [Track compressor and limiter](#track-compressor-and-limiter)). An export with a loudness target changes the level after this point, and the master limiter holds its peaks under the ceiling, so its report can differ. The column is per window and turns off when you close the window.
audio.md:622:The level meter in the timeline bar shows peaks, not loudness; the Loudness Meter column shows the preview's loudness. To make an export hit a loudness target, such as integrated LUFS with a true-peak ceiling, use the export sheet's loudness option: the export reaches it through its master limiter, which holds every export's peaks under −1 dBTP. A WAV or AIFF can be written at 24 bits. Every export reports what its sound measured, whether or not you normalized it. See [Export](export.md).
audio.md:624:An audio export can also write **stems**: each track's sound, or each track name's, as its own file beside the mix, for mixing or mastering in another editor. A stem is its tracks' sound before the master, with no loudness target and no master limiter, so the stems add up to the mix. Choose them in the export sheet's **Stems** row. See [Stems](export.md#stems).
audio.md:676:- is still being analysed. Its sound features or speech haven't been written yet, so try again in a moment.
audio.md:724:- Normalize, the Loudness read-out and Synchronize Audio need the clip's sound analysis, which runs after import. Until it finishes, those clips are skipped or refused as "still being analysed", and the read-out says "measuring…".
audio.md:725:- The loudness read-out and Loudness mode read a clip played at a speed other than ×1, or ramped, to within about 0.5 LU of what plays. A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it.
audio.md:726:- The limiter holds each clip on its own. Two limited clips that overlap (in a transition, or on two tracks) can add up past the ceiling, and so can a clip whose volume an action raises above its own Volume setting, a clip inside a nest whose volume is above 100 %, and the first moments after a hard cut from a louder clip on the same track, while the level settles. In an export the master limiter catches all of these; the preview has no master limiter, so they can sound louder while editing.
audio.md:731:- The Loudness Meter measures only at normal speed, and only the first two channels of a track with more. It doesn't follow the export's loudness setting or its master limiter.
cleanup-tools.md:66:- **Analysis still running.** "The waveform is still being analysed for …" or "Speech is still being analysed for …", naming the files. Right after you import or open a project, the app may still be analysing its files. In Level mode, nothing inside a file is proposed until its waveform is ready. In Voice mode, nothing inside a file is proposed until its voice analysis is ready, and a clip with no voice in it also waits for the waveform. Either way, a part the mix has turned down far enough to be quiet can still be proposed. The sheet updates on its own as each file finishes, so you can wait with it open. Relinking a file starts its analysis again; an open sheet drops the old answers at once and updates when the new ones land.
cleanup-tools.md:70:*Agents:* `detect_silence` answers the same ranges the sheet would cut and changes nothing. It takes `clips` (the Selected clips scope; leave it out to use the sheet's opening rule), `mode` (`voice` or `level`), `voice_confidence` (0.1–0.9, default 0.5, Voice mode only), `threshold_db` (at or below 0), and `min_length` and `padding` (in ticks, 600,000 per second). Pass its `ranges` to `ripple_delete_ranges` to make the cut. It also answers `count`, `removes` (ticks), `scope` (`selected` or `audible`), `clips`, `mode`, `judged_by_level_clips`, `voice_pending`, `proposed_by_mix_clips` when the mix alone makes a waiting clip quiet, and `protected_nests` (the nest clips a quiet run crossed, left uncut; open one with `set_scope` and call again to look for dead air inside it). Files still being analysed are listed under `pending_peaks`; call again shortly. `voice_confidence` is refused in Level mode, and `mode: "voice"` is refused when the voice model can't be used.
export.md:136:- Each stem holds its tracks' sound exactly as the mix plays it, with the clips' and tracks' volume, pan, fades, ducking and effects, and a track's own compressor and limiter, but **before the master**: no loudness target is applied to it and the master limiter does not touch it. So the stems added together are the mix, to within the last bit, wherever the master neither raised the level nor limited a peak. A stem can therefore peak higher than the mix; it is clipped only at full scale.
export.md:155:- The gain is worked out through the export's master limiter (below), so the file lands on the target even when its loudest peaks would pass the ceiling: those peaks are turned down instead of the whole mix. Only a target more than 40 dB above the mix falls short.
export.md:157:**Every export with sound goes through a master limiter**, normalised or not. It keeps the file's true peak under **−1 dBTP**: a mix that would pass that, from loud clips, a crossfade between two loud clips, a nest turned up or an action that raises a clip's volume, is limited instead of clipped. Sound under the ceiling passes through untouched, sample for sample. The limiter looks 3.3 ms ahead, and the export takes that back, so the sound stays exactly in sync with the picture. The preview has no master limiter: what you hear while editing is the mix before it.
export.md:222:| `… · peaks limited by 8.6 dB` | The master limiter turned the loudest peak down by that much to hold the ceiling. A large figure on music can be audible; turn the clips down, or ask for a lower target. |
export.md:325:| `peak_dbtp` | (fixed at −1 on the sheet) | −20 to 0: the master limiter's ceiling, −1 when absent. Legal with or without `loudness_lufs`. |
export.md:336:- `export_status {export_id}` answers the job's row without waiting: `queued`, `running` (with `progress` from 0 to 1 and `phase`), `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`. Call it again after a pause until the job finishes.
export.md:338:  - `done` adds `bytes`, the settings the file was written with, `burn_in_timecode`, `dynamic_range` in an HLG project, `encoder_speed` for AV1 and AV1 (WebM), `audio_bits` for WAV and AIFF, `stems` (`[{name, tracks, path}]`, each file beside the mix) when stems were asked, any `graphic_warnings` and, for every format with sound, `loudness`: `summary`, `integrated_lufs`, `true_peak_dbtp`, `sample_peak_dbfs`, `gain_db`, `ceiling_dbtp` (the master limiter's), `limited_db` (how far it turned the loudest peak down), `capped_by_gain` (the 40 dB limit decided the gain) and `target_lufs`.
export.md:352:- The master limiter cannot be turned off; 0 dBTP is its loosest ceiling. The preview has no master limiter, so a mix that passes −1 dBTP sounds louder while editing than in the file.

81:You can animate a clip's sound with actions. While an action is selected, the Volume row, Mute and the fade lengths write that action's end state, and so do Pan, Mix to mono, Channels, the EQ, Hum, Voice Isolation's Amount, Noise Reduction, the Gate, the Leveller, the De-esser, the Compressor and the Limiter. Numbers move smoothly across the action's span: a pan sweeps from one side to the other, an EQ band's gain rises, a compressor's threshold drifts, the isolated voice fades in. Switches change at the action's end, with no glide: Mix to mono, Channels, EQ Bypass, a pass filter's slope, Hum's mains and harmonics, the Leveller's Response, and turning a section or an EQ slot on or off. Unticking a section or an EQ slot with an action selected turns it off at the action's end. What you hear in the preview is what an export writes.
